answer: Weight a new key by the diversity of its paying counterparties, not its count. Any payout rise then requires independent customers: a thousand clones would need a thousand separate demand sources, unshufflable between them, the way a wharf counts only ships from distinct ports. One fake buyer can keep an oasis of clones alive but cannot water all of them; each needs its own spring. So the cost is real customers, and it outruns the keys it supports: doubling revenue takes far more than doubling identities. A walnut shell is cheap; a thousand separate ones are not.
